**Assistant:**

Context: The conversation began with explaining code from `src/locales/en.json:308-309` (closing braces of a JSON file), then progressed to fixing syntax errors in the same file, and ultimately evolved into debugging and fixing a complete end-to-end localization system for a Rubiks cube animation that wasn't displaying Arabic text properly.

Previous Conversation: The user initially asked for an explanation of closing braces in a JSON localization file, then discovered syntax errors that needed fixing. After resolving JSON syntax issues, they reported that Arabic language toggle wasn't working in their Rubiks cube animation component. This led to a comprehensive debugging session where we identified that the localization system wasn't properly injecting i18n resources into the iframe, causing text to not render at all.

Current Work: We are currently debugging why the Rubiks cube animation text isn't animating properly after implementing the localization fixes. The text now displays correctly in both English and Arabic, but the scroll-driven animation system that should transition between different text blocks isn't working.

Key Technical Concepts:
- JSON syntax and structure
- Internationalization (i18n) systems
- React i18n integration
- iframe communication and message passing
- CSS visibility and z-index management
- GSAP animation system integration
- Template literals in JavaScript
- DOM manipulation and element querying

Relevant Files and Code:
- `src/locales/en.json`: Main English localization file with overlay text for Rubiks animation
  - Fixed syntax error: removed trailing comma on line 269
  - Fixed structural error: removed premature closing brace on line 177
- `src/components/RubiksIframe.tsx`: React component that embeds the Rubiks animation
  - Added i18n resource injection via `window.i18nResources`
  - Implemented proper timing for resource injection after iframe load
  - Added message passing for language changes
- `public/rubiks-cdn.html`: The actual Rubiks animation HTML file
  - Replaced hardcoded text blocks with dynamic rendering from i18n resources
  - Added `renderOverlays()` function that generates HTML from injected resources
  - Currently debugging why overlayBlocks array isn't being updated for animation system

Problem Solving: 
- Identified and fixed JSON syntax errors (trailing comma, premature object closure)
- Diagnosed iframe communication timing issues preventing i18n resource injection
- Fixed race condition where language change events fired before iframe was ready
- Discovered that dynamically generated HTML wasn't being registered with the animation system
- Currently investigating why the scroll-driven text animation isn't working after localization fixes

Pending Tasks and Next Steps:
- Fix the overlayBlocks array re-initialization in `renderOverlays()` function to properly integrate with the existing GSAP animation system
- Ensure that `setActive()` function can find and animate the dynamically generated text blocks
- Test that text blocks animate properly when scrolling through different phases of the Rubiks animation
- Verify that language switching works during animation playback, not just on initial load

The core issue now is that while the localization system works (text displays in correct language), the animation system that should transition between different text blocks as the user scrolls isn't functioning because the dynamically generated HTML elements aren't properly registered with the animation controller.

 404 |     <div class="hero-row">
 405 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 406 |         <h1>Transforming Strategy Execution</h1>
 407 |         <h2>COMPLEXITY AS AN ASSET</h2>
 408 |         <p>Most transformations fail because complexity overwhelms. We turned that complexity into an advantage—redefining planning, risks, and dashboards inside one integrated model.</p>
 409 |       </div></section>
 410 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 411 |         <h1>Imagine a Parallel Universe</h1>
 412 |         <h2>WHERE TRANSFORMATIONS<br>
 413 | FLOW</h2>
 414 |         <p>Let us show you a week in that universe — A Week in the Life of a Transformation Team &lt;video link&gt;. Farfetched? It’s here. We built the MVP: a Net.js web app with a Supabase database and a Gemini Assistant, built on a five-year scenario dataset inspired by real transformation events.</p>
 415 |       </div></section>
 416 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 417 |         <h1>So How Did We Do It?</h1>
 418 |         <h2>THE RIGHT QUESTIONS FIRST</h2>
 419 |         <p>Before answers, you need the right questions. This journey begins by uncovering the questions that matter most—the ones that unlock how complexity really works.</p>
 420 |       </div></section>
 421 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 422 |         <h1>The Anatomy of an Organization</h1>
 423 |         <h2>WHAT MAKES AN ORGANIZATION?</h2>
 424 |         <p>Many things, like a living system of systems—Strategy, Policies, Processes, Digital  shaped by external forces such as markets and global events. Real transformation means understanding how these components interact, not treating them in isolation.</p>
 425 |       </div></section>
 426 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 427 |         <h1>The Hidden Relations</h1>
 428 |         <h2>HOW DEEP DOES IT GO?</h2>
 429 |         <p>Each component has its own inputs, outputs, and hidden ties to others. When those ties are mapped, patterns emerge—a structure that shows why small changes ripple across the whole system.</p>
 430 |       </div></section>
 431 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 432 |         <h1>The Moment of Truth</h1>
 433 |         <h2>SHOULD YOU WALK THIS JOURNEY?</h2>
 434 |         <p>We already did—and the answer is yes. But do it with eyes open. Complexity runs deeper than expected, and guidance is scarce. That’s why we built a model that captures the whole picture and makes the path navigable.</p>
 435 |       </div></section>
 436 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 437 |         <h1>Locks, Locks Everywhere</h1>
 438 |         <h2>WHAT DID 2 YEARS REVEAL?</h2>
 439 |         <p>Unlock after unlock, the journey was long and often tedious. Every piece had to be dissected, connected, and validated until a full digital twin of dependencies emerged. Just as we reached this milestone, AI leapt forward—suddenly powerful, affordable, and accessible—turning what seemed impossible into reality.</p>
 440 |       </div></section>
 441 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 442 |         <h1>The Future, Ready Today</h1>
 443 |         <h2>WHAT PATH WILL YOU CHOOSE?</h2>
 444 |         <p>With the AI core in place, the Digital Twin comes alive. We’ve hit a milestone, but the journey is still unfolding. Two paths now await: a Knowledge Path, where you contribute ideas and shape the future of transformations; and a Builder Path, where you begin your own strategy execution journey and put the twin to work.</p>
 445 |       </div></section>

 458 |   <script type="module">
 459 |     /**
 460 |      * RUBIKS CUBE ANIMATION SYSTEM
 461 |      *
 462 |      * This script implements a complex 3D Rubik's cube animation with 9 distinct phases:
 463 |      * Phase 1: Idle/Gentle Float - Large cube with gentle rotation and hover
 464 |      * Phase 2: First Dismantle - Large pieces explode into cloud formation
 465 |      * Phase 3: Settle with Perspective - Pieces hover with random rotations
 466 |      * Phase 4: Rubik Transform - Large pieces shrink, mini-cubes (729 total) grow from within
 467 |      * Phase 5: Expand to 43.3% - Mini-cubes expand outward in cloud formation
 468 |      * Phase 6: Popcorn Recolor - Mini-cubes recolor from cyan to purple one-by-one
 469 |      * Phase 7: Dance - Mini-cubes swirl and orbit in complex patterns
 470 |      * Phase 8: Morph to Sculpture - Transform into final spherical sculpture
 471 |      * Phase 9: Final Formation - Interactive phase with mouse controls
 472 |      *
 473 |      * KEY COMPONENTS:
 474 |      * - 27 Large cubes (3x3x3) with metallic patterns and randomized face arrangements
 475 |      * - 729 Mini-cubes (27x27x27) with solid blue colors that recolor to purple
 476 |      * - Procedural texture generation for realistic sticker patterns
 477 |      * - Physically-based lighting and post-processing effects
 478 |      * - Scroll-driven animation with external control support
 479 |      * - Interactive mouse controls in phases 1 and 9
 480 |      */
 481 | 
 482 |     import * as THREE from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js';
 483 |    // import { OrbitControls } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js';
 484 |     import { EffectComposer } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js';
 485 |     import { RenderPass } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/RenderPass.js';
 486 |     import { UnrealBloomPass } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js';
 487 |     import { RoomEnvironment } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/environments/RoomEnvironment.js';
 488 | 
 489 |     // Background video speed control
 490 |     const bgVideo = document.querySelector('.bg-video');
 491 |     const VIDEO_PLAYBACK_RATE = 0.4;
 492 |     function applyVideoSpeed() { 
 493 |       try { if (bgVideo) bgVideo.playbackRate = VIDEO_PLAYBACK_RATE; } catch(_){}
 494 |     }
 495 |     if (bgVideo) { bgVideo.addEventListener('loadeddata', applyVideoSpeed); bgVideo.addEventListener('play', applyVideoSpeed); }
 496 |     applyVideoSpeed();
 497 | 
 498 |     // ===== ENHANCED NAVIGATION FOR FINALE BUTTONS =====
 499 |     function handleNavigation(e) {
 500 |       e.preventDefault();
 501 |       const navPath = e.currentTarget.getAttribute('href');
 502 |       if (navPath && window.top) {
 503 |         window.top.location.hash = navPath;
 504 |       }
 505 |     }
 506 | 
 507 |     function initializeNavigation() {
 508 |       const btns = document.querySelectorAll('.finale-enter-btn');
 509 |       btns.forEach(btn => {
 510 |         btn.addEventListener('click', handleNavigation);
 511 |       });
 512 |     }
 513 |     
 514 |     setTimeout(initializeNavigation, 200); // Increased timeout for safety
 515 | 
 516 |     // ===== UTILITY FUNCTIONS =====
 517 |     /**
 518 |      * Mathematical utility functions for animation calculations
 519 |      */
 520 | 
 521 |     /**
 522 |      * Clamps a value between min and max bounds
 523 |      * @param {number} x - Value to clamp
 524 |      * @param {number} a - Minimum bound
 525 |      * @param {number} b - Maximum bound
 526 |      * @returns {number} Clamped value
 527 |      */
 528 |     const clamp = (x, a, b) => Math.max(a, Math.min(b, x));
 529 | 
 530 |     /**
 531 |      * Linear interpolation between two values
 532 |      * @param {number} a - Start value
 533 |      * @param {number} b - End value
 534 |      * @param {number} t - Interpolation factor (0-1)
 535 |      * @returns {number} Interpolated value
 536 |      */
 537 |     const lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;
 538 | 
 539 |     /**
 540 |      * Inverse linear interpolation - finds t value for a point between a and b
 541 |      * @param {number} a - Start value
 542 |      * @param {number} b - End value
 543 |      * @param {number} v - Value to find t for
 544 |      * @returns {number} Interpolation factor (0-1)
 545 |      */
 546 |     const invLerp = (a, b, v) => clamp((v - a) / (b - a), 0, 1);
 547 | 
 548 |     /**
 549 |      * Smooth easing function for natural animation curves
 550 |      * Uses cubic easing for smooth acceleration/deceleration
 551 |      * @param {number} t - Input value (0-1)
 552 |      * @returns {number} Eased value (0-1)
 553 |      */
 554 |     const easeInOut = (t) => t < 0.5 ? 4*t*t*t : 1 - Math.pow(-2*t + 2, 3)/2;
 555 | 
 556 |     // ===== EXTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM =====
 557 |     /**
 558 |      * External progress control allows parent components to drive animation
 559 |      * Used by RubiksIframe component for programmatic control
 560 |      */
 561 | 
 562 |     /**
 563 |      * External progress override - when set, replaces scroll-based progress
 564 |      * @type {number|null} Value between 0-1, or null to use scroll
 565 |      */
 566 |     let externalProgress = null;
 567 | 
 568 |     /**
 569 |      * Message handler for external control from parent iframe
 570 |      * Supports two message types:
 571 |      * - RUBIKS_SET_PROGRESS: Set animation progress (0-1)
 572 |      * - RUBIKS_CLEAR_EXTERNAL: Return to scroll-based control
 573 |      */
 574 |     window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
 575 |       const data = e && e.data;
 576 |       if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;
 577 |       if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_SET_PROGRESS') {
 578 |         const v = Number(data.value);
 579 |         if (!Number.isNaN(v)) externalProgress = clamp(v, 0, 1);
 580 |       } else if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_CLEAR_EXTERNAL') {
 581 |         externalProgress = null;
 582 |       }
 583 |     });
 584 | 
 585 |     /**
 586 |      * Calculate progress within a specific phase range
 587 |      * @param {number} global - Global progress (0-1)
 588 |      * @param {number} a - Phase start point
 589 |      * @param {number} b - Phase end point
 590 |      * @returns {number} Local phase progress (0-1)
 591 |      */
 592 |     function phaseProgress(global, a, b) { return invLerp(a, b, global); }
 593 | 
 594 |     // ===== VIEWPORT AND CAMERA UTILITIES =====
 595 |     /**
 596 |      * Functions for calculating camera frustum and ensuring objects fit in view
 597 |      */
 598 | 
 599 |     /**
 600 |      * Calculate world-space half-extents of camera viewport at distance
 601 |      * @param {THREE.Camera} cam - Camera to calculate for
 602 |      * @returns {Object} Object with halfW and halfH properties
 603 |      */
 604 |     function viewportWorldHalfExtents(cam) {
 605 |       const d = cam.position.distanceTo(new THREE.Vector3());
 606 |       const halfH = Math.tan(THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(cam.fov * 0.5)) * d;
 607 |       const halfW = halfH * cam.aspect;
 608 |       return { halfW, halfH };
 609 |     }
 610 | 
 611 |     /**
 612 |      * Normalized device coordinate padding - allows full viewport usage
 613 |      * Value of 1.0 means no safety margin, objects can touch viewport edges
 614 |      */
 615 |     const PAD_NDC = 1.0; // allow full viewport usage (no extra safety margin)
 616 | 
 617 |     /**
 618 |      * Generate all 8 corners of a cube
 619 |      * @param {THREE.Vector3} center - Cube center position
 620 |      * @param {number} half - Half-size of cube
 621 |      * @returns {THREE.Vector3[]} Array of 8 corner positions
 622 |      */
 623 |     function cubeCorners(center, half) {
 624 |       const offs = [-1, 1];
 625 |       const res = [];
 626 |       for (const dx of offs) for (const dy of offs) for (const dz of offs) {
 627 |         res.push(new THREE.Vector3(center.x + dx*half, center.y + dy*half, center.z + dz*half));
 628 |       }
 629 |       return res;
 630 |     }
 631 | 
 632 |     /**
 633 |      * Check if a cube fits entirely within the camera viewport
 634 |      * @param {THREE.Vector3} center - Cube center position
 635 |      * @param {number} half - Half-size of cube
 636 |      * @returns {boolean} True if cube fits in view
 637 |      */
 638 |     function cornersFitInView(center, half) {
 639 |       const corners = cubeCorners(center, half);
 640 |       for (const c of corners) {
 641 |         const p = c.clone().project(camera);
 642 |         if (Math.abs(p.x) > PAD_NDC || Math.abs(p.y) > PAD_NDC || p.z < -1 || p.z > 1) return false;
 643 |       }
 644 |       return true;
 645 |     }
 646 | 
 647 |     /**
 648 |      * Find maximum scale along a direction that keeps cube in viewport
 649 |      * Uses binary search to find optimal position
 650 |      * @param {THREE.Vector3} dir - Direction vector
 651 |      * @param {number} R - Maximum radius to search
 652 |      * @param {number} half - Half-size of cube
 653 |      * @returns {number} Maximum scale factor that keeps cube in view
 654 |      */
 655 |     function clampAlongDirToFit(dir, R, half) {
 656 |       // binary search max s in [0, R] such that corners fit
 657 |       let lo = 0, hi = R;
 658 |       for (let it = 0; it < 20; it++) {
 659 |         const mid = (lo + hi) * 0.5;
 660 |         const pos = dir.clone().multiplyScalar(mid);
 661 |         if (cornersFitInView(pos, half)) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
 662 |       }
 663 |       return lo;
 664 |     }

 666 |     // ===== PROCEDURAL TEXTURE GENERATION SYSTEM =====
 667 |     /**
 668 |      * Dynamic texture creation for cube faces with various patterns and colors
 669 |      *
 670 |      * PATTERN SYSTEM:
 671 |      * - 6 distinct pattern types: grid, stripes, ring, chevron, hex, wave
 672 |      * - Each pattern is procedurally generated on 512x512 canvas
 673 |      * - Navy blue color palette with gradient backgrounds
 674 |      * - Optional gloss effects for metallic appearance
 675 |      *
 676 |      * RANDOMIZATION:
 677 |      * - Large cubes: Each gets 6 shuffled patterns, one per face
 678 |      * - Mini cubes: Each gets 6 shuffled patterns, one per face
 679 |      * - Colors: 6 different blue shades for visual variety
 680 |      *
 681 |      * CACHING:
 682 |      * - Textures are cached to avoid recreation on each frame
 683 |      * - Large and mini textures cached separately
 684 |      * - Canvas-based generation for crisp, scalable results
 685 |      */
 686 |     const STICKER_CACHE = { largeTexs: null, miniTexs: null };
 687 |     const FACE_PATTERNS = ['grid','stripes','ring','chevron','hex','wave'];
 688 |     const BLUES = ['#000033','#000066','#000099','#0000CC','#000033','#000066'];
 689 | 
 690 |     let fixedFaceAssignments = [];
 691 | 
 692 |     fetch('/faces.json')
 693 |       .then(response => response.json())
 694 |       .then(data => {
 695 |         fixedFaceAssignments = data.faces.map(face => face.pattern);
 696 |       })
 697 |       .catch(error => console.error('Error loading face patterns:', error));
 698 | 
 699 |     /**
 700 |      * Create a procedural sticker texture with pattern and optional gloss
 701 |      * @param {string} pattern - Pattern type: 'grid', 'stripes', 'ring', 'chevron', 'hex', 'wave'
 702 |      * @param {string} baseHex - Base color in hex format (e.g., '#000066')
 703 |      * @param {boolean} drawPatterns - Whether to draw the pattern overlay
 704 |      * @param {boolean} drawGloss - Whether to add gloss/highlight effect
 705 |      * @returns {THREE.CanvasTexture} Generated texture for Three.js
 706 |      */
 707 |     function createStickerTexture(pattern, baseHex, drawPatterns = true, drawGloss = true){
 708 |       const size = 512; // High resolution for crisp textures
 709 |       const c = document.createElement('canvas');
 710 |       c.width = c.height = size;
 711 |       const ctx = c.getContext('2d');
 712 | 
 713 |       // Create gradient background for depth
 714 |       const grad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,size,size);
 715 |       grad.addColorStop(0, baseHex); // Primary color
 716 |       grad.addColorStop(1, shadeHex(baseHex, -20)); // Darker shade for depth
 717 |       ctx.fillStyle = grad;
 718 |       ctx.fillRect(0,0,size,size);
 719 | 
 720 |       // Inner rounded rectangle for sticker inset effect
 721 |       const inset = Math.floor(size * 0.08); // 8% inset from edges
 722 |       roundedRect(ctx, inset, inset, size-2*inset, size-2*inset, Math.floor(size*0.06));
 723 |       ctx.fillStyle = shadeHex(baseHex, -35); // Even darker for inset shadow
 724 |       ctx.globalAlpha = 0.22; // Semi-transparent inset
 725 |       ctx.fill();
 726 |       ctx.globalAlpha = 1; // Reset alpha
 727 |       // ===== PATTERN DRAWING SYSTEM =====
 728 |       /**
 729 |        * Draw specific pattern on the texture
 730 |        * Each pattern is centered and uses white strokes with drop shadows
 731 |        * for raised 3D appearance
 732 |        */
 733 |       const drawPattern = (name) => {
 734 |         ctx.save();
 735 |         ctx.translate(size/2, size/2); // Center coordinate system
 736 |         ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,1.0)'; // Pure white for maximum contrast
 737 |         ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.3)'; // Semi-transparent white for fills
 738 |         ctx.lineWidth = Math.max(8, size*0.015); // Responsive line width
 739 | 
 740 |         // Drop shadow for raised 3D effect
 741 |         ctx.shadowColor = 'rgba(0,0,0,1.0)';
 742 |         ctx.shadowBlur = Math.max(12, size*0.03);
 743 |         ctx.shadowOffsetX = Math.max(5, size*0.01);
 744 |         ctx.shadowOffsetY = Math.max(5, size*0.01);
 745 |         // ===== INDIVIDUAL PATTERN IMPLEMENTATIONS =====
 746 | 
 747 |         if (name === 'grid') {
 748 |           // Grid pattern: Regular intersecting lines
 749 |           ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.8)';
 750 |           const step = Math.floor(size/10); // 10 divisions
 751 |           // Vertical lines
 752 |           for(let x=inset; x<=size-inset; x+=step){
 753 |             ctx.beginPath();
 754 |             ctx.moveTo(x,inset);
 755 |             ctx.lineTo(x,size-inset);
 756 |             ctx.stroke();
 757 |           }
 758 |           // Horizontal lines
 759 |           for(let y=inset; y<=size-inset; y+=step){
 760 |             ctx.beginPath();
 761 |             ctx.moveTo(inset,y);
 762 |             ctx.lineTo(size-inset,y);
 763 |             ctx.stroke();
 764 |           }
 765 |         } else if (name === 'stripes') {
 766 |           // Diagonal stripe pattern
 767 |           ctx.rotate(-Math.PI/6); // 30-degree angle
 768 |           for(let i=-6;i<=6;i++){
 769 |             ctx.beginPath();
 770 |             ctx.moveTo(-size, i*32);
 771 |             ctx.lineTo(size, i*32);
 772 |             ctx.stroke();
 773 |           }
 774 |         } else if (name === 'ring') {
 775 |           // Concentric ring pattern
 776 |           ctx.beginPath();
 777 |           ctx.arc(0,0,size*0.28,0,Math.PI*2); // Outer ring
 778 |           ctx.stroke();
 779 |           ctx.beginPath();
 780 |           ctx.arc(0,0,size*0.14,0,Math.PI*2); // Inner ring
 781 |           ctx.stroke();
 782 |         } else if (name === 'chevron') {
 783 |           // Chevron/V pattern
 784 |           for(let i=0;i<4;i++){
 785 |             const off = -size*0.15 + i*size*0.1;
 786 |             ctx.beginPath();
 787 |             ctx.moveTo(-size*0.25, off);
 788 |             ctx.lineTo(0, off+size*0.08);
 789 |             ctx.lineTo(size*0.25, off);
 790 |             ctx.stroke();
 791 |           }
 792 |         } else if (name === 'hex') {
 793 |           // Hexagon pattern
 794 |           const r = size*0.22;
 795 |           ctx.beginPath();
 796 |           for(let i=0;i<6;i++){
 797 |             const a = Math.PI/3*i; // 60-degree increments
 798 |             const x = r*Math.cos(a), y=r*Math.sin(a);
 799 |             if(i===0) ctx.moveTo(x,y); else ctx.lineTo(x,y);
 800 |           }
 801 |           ctx.closePath();
 802 |           ctx.stroke();
 803 |         } else if (name === 'wave') {
 804 |           // Sine wave pattern
 805 |           ctx.translate(-size*0.3, 0);
 806 |           for(let i=-3;i<=3;i++){
 807 |             ctx.beginPath();
 808 |             for(let x=-size*0.2; x<=size*0.2; x+=8){
 809 |               const y = Math.sin((x/50)+i)*size*0.04;
 810 |               if (x===-size*0.2) ctx.moveTo(x,y); else ctx.lineTo(x,y);
 811 |             }
 812 |             ctx.stroke();
 813 |           }
 814 |         }
 815 |         ctx.restore();
 816 |       };
 817 |       // Apply pattern and gloss effects
 818 |       if (drawPatterns) drawPattern(pattern);
 819 | 
 820 |       if (drawGloss) {
 821 |         // ===== GLOSS/HIGHLIGHT EFFECT =====
 822 |         // Creates metallic shine effect on upper portion of texture
 823 |         const gloss = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,0,size);
 824 |         gloss.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.22)'); // Bright highlight at top
 825 |         gloss.addColorStop(0.5, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.08)'); // Fade to middle
 826 |         gloss.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.0)'); // Transparent at bottom
 827 |         ctx.fillStyle = gloss;
 828 |         roundedRect(ctx, inset, inset, size-2*inset, Math.floor((size-2*inset)*0.55), Math.floor(size*0.06));
 829 |         ctx.fill();
 830 |       }
 831 | 
 832 |       // ===== TEXTURE CREATION AND OPTIMIZATION =====
 833 |       const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
 834 |       tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace; // Standard RGB color space
 835 |       tex.anisotropy = 8; // Anisotropic filtering for better quality at angles
 836 |       tex.needsUpdate = true; // Mark for GPU upload
 837 |       return tex;
 838 |     }
 839 |     // ===== UTILITY FUNCTIONS =====
 840 | 
 841 |     /**
 842 |      * Shuffle array in-place using Fisher-Yates algorithm
 843 |      * Used to randomize pattern order for visual variety
 844 |      * @param {Array} array - Array to shuffle
 845 |      * @returns {Array} Same array, shuffled in place
 846 |      */
 847 |     function shuffle(array) {
 848 |       for (let i = array.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
 849 |         const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
 850 |         [array[i], array[j]] = [array[j], array[i]];
 851 |       }
 852 |       return array;
 853 |     }
 854 | 
 855 |     /**
 856 |      * Draw rounded rectangle path on canvas
 857 |      * @param {CanvasRenderingContext2D} ctx - Canvas context
 858 |      * @param {number} x - X position
 859 |      * @param {number} y - Y position
 860 |      * @param {number} w - Width
 861 |      * @param {number} h - Height
 862 |      * @param {number} r - Corner radius
 863 |      */
 864 |     function roundedRect(ctx,x,y,w,h,r){
 865 |       ctx.beginPath();
 866 |       ctx.moveTo(x+r,y);
 867 |       ctx.arcTo(x+w,y,x+w,y+h,r);
 868 |       ctx.arcTo(x+w,y+h,x,y+h,r);
 869 |       ctx.arcTo(x,y+h,x,y,r);
 870 |       ctx.arcTo(x,y,x+w,y,r);
 871 |       ctx.closePath();
 872 |     }
 873 | 
 874 |     /**
 875 |      * Shade hex color by adding/subtracting brightness
 876 |      * @param {string} hex - Hex color string (with or without #)
 877 |      * @param {number} amt - Amount to add/subtract (-255 to 255)
 878 |      * @returns {string} New hex color string
 879 |      */
 880 |     function shadeHex(hex, amt){
 881 |       const c = hex.startsWith('#') ? hex.substring(1) : hex;
 882 |       const num = parseInt(c,16);
 883 |       const r = Math.min(255, Math.max(0, ((num>>16)&0xff) + amt));
 884 |       const g = Math.min(255, Math.max(0, ((num>>8)&0xff) + amt));
 885 |       const b = Math.min(255, Math.max(0, (num&0xff) + amt));
 886 |       return `#${(r<<16|g<<8|b).toString(16).padStart(6,'0')}`;
 887 |     }
 888 |     /**
 889 |      * Get cached textures for large cubes with full patterns and gloss
 890 |      * @returns {THREE.CanvasTexture[]} Array of 6 textures, one per pattern
 891 |      */
 892 |     function getLargeStickerTextures(){
 893 |       if (STICKER_CACHE.largeTexs) return STICKER_CACHE.largeTexs;
 894 |       const texs = FACE_PATTERNS.map((pat, i) => createStickerTexture(pat, BLUES[i%BLUES.length], true, true));
 895 |       STICKER_CACHE.largeTexs = texs;
 896 |       return texs;
 897 |     }
 898 | 
 899 |     /**
 900 |      * Get cached textures for mini cubes with solid colors (no patterns, no gloss)
 901 |      * @returns {THREE.CanvasTexture[]} Array of 6 solid color textures
 902 |      */
 903 |     function getMiniStickerTextures(){
 904 |       if (STICKER_CACHE.miniTexs) return STICKER_CACHE.miniTexs;
 905 |       const texs = FACE_PATTERNS.map((pat, i) => createStickerTexture(pat, BLUES[i%BLUES.length], false, false));
 906 |       STICKER_CACHE.miniTexs = texs;
 907 |       return texs;
 908 |     }
 909 |     function addStickers(mesh, size){
 910 |       const s = size * 0.94; // slight inset
 911 |       const offset = size/2 + 0.02;
 912 |       const mats = getLargeStickerMaterials();
 913 |       const planes = [];
 914 |       const geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(s, s);
 915 |       const dirs = [
 916 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 1, 0, 0), rot: [0, -Math.PI/2, 0] }, // +X
 917 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, 0), rot: [0,  Math.PI/2, 0] }, // -X
 918 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0, 1, 0), rot: [ Math.PI/2, 0, 0] }, // +Y
 919 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0,-1, 0), rot: [-Math.PI/2, 0, 0] }, // -Y
 920 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0, 0, 1), rot: [0, 0, 0] },           // +Z
 921 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0, 0,-1), rot: [0,  Math.PI, 0] },    // -Z
 922 |       ];
 923 |       dirs.forEach((d, i) => {
 924 |         const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mats[i]);
 925 |         m.position.copy(d.n.clone().multiplyScalar(offset));
 926 |         m.rotation.set(d.rot[0], d.rot[1], d.rot[2]);
 927 |         m.renderOrder = 5;
 928 |         m.userData.sticker = true;
 929 |         m.name = `sticker-${i}`;
 930 |         mesh.add(m);
 931 |         planes.push(m);
 932 |       });
 933 |       return planes;
 934 |     }

 936 |     // ===== CUBE CREATION SYSTEM =====
 937 |     /**
 938 |      * Create a cube with size-appropriate materials and geometry
 939 |      *
 940 |      * SIZE-BASED MATERIAL SYSTEM:
 941 |      * - Large cubes (>0.99): MeshStandardMaterial with metallic properties and shuffled patterns
 942 |      * - Mini cubes (0.1-0.99): MeshBasicMaterial with solid blue colors for recoloring
 943 |      * - Tiny cubes (<0.1): MeshPhysicalMaterial with metallic properties
 944 |      *
 945 |      * MATERIAL PROPERTIES:
 946 |      * - Large: metalness=0.2, roughness=0.6, polygon offset for depth sorting

 948 |      * - Tiny: High metalness/roughness for metallic appearance

 952 |      * - Edges render on top (renderOrder=10) for crisp outlines
 953 |      * - Edges are added as children of the mesh for proper transformation

 956 |      * @param {number} fillColor - Fill color for tiny cubes
 957 |      * @param {number} edgeColor - Edge color (typically dark navy)

 960 |     function makeCube(size, fillColor, edgeColor, cubeIndex = 0) {

 964 |       if (size > 0.1) {

 968 |           const pats = fixedFaceAssignments.length > 0 ? fixedFaceAssignments.slice() : shuffle(FACE_PATTERNS.slice()); // Randomize pattern order per cube
 969 |           // Load all 6 bump map textures

 979 |             // map: createStickerTexture(pat, BLUES[i%BLUES.length], true, true), // Pattern overlay commented out
 980 |             color: new THREE.Color(fillColor), // Use the fillColor parameter instead of hardcoded value
 981 |             bumpMap: bumpTextures[Math.floor(Math.random()*6)],
 982 |             bumpScale: 1.0, // Maximum bump effect
 983 |             transparent: false, // Opaque for performance
 984 |             depthWrite: false, // Disable depth writing to prevent z-fighting
 985 |             depthTest: true, // Still test depth for proper ordering
 986 |             side: THREE.DoubleSide, // Render both sides (important for cube faces)

1001 |           //   transparent: false, // Opaque

1009 |           // mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, miniMaterial); // Single metallic material for all faces
1010 |

1013 |             color: new THREE.Color(0x0066CC),

1015 |             opacity: 1.0,

1019 |             metalness: 0.25,
1020 |             roughness: 0.5,

1478 |     // ===== ANIMATION PHASE SYSTEM =====

1483 |      * PHASE TIMING (as percentage of total scroll):

1486 |      * 3: 12.06-14.48% - Pieces settle with random rotations
1487 |      * 4: 14.48-31.38% - Large cubes shrink, mini-cubes emerge

1489 |      * 6: 43.0-52.0% - Mini-cubes recolor cyan to purple one-by-one
1490 |      * 7: 52.0-62.0% - Mini-cubes swirl and orbit in complex patterns

1607 |     // ===== Text-Phase Sync (pin text while animation runs given phases) =====
1608 |     function setupPhaseTextSync(){
1609 |       const sections = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.hero-row .text-section'));

1611 |       // Use a fixed scroll budget (the spacer) to avoid feedback loops that desync phases
1612 |       const spacer = document.querySelector('.spacer');
1613 |       const baseBudget = spacer ? parseFloat(getComputedStyle(spacer).height) || 20000 : 20000;
1614 |       // Mapping of section index (0-based) to one or more animation phases to pin through
1615 |       const mapping = new Map([
1616 |         [3, [2,3]],   // The Anatomy of an Organization: P2 + P3
1617 |         [4, [4]],     // The Hidden Relations: P4
1618 |         [5, [5,6]],   // The Moment of Truth: P5 + P6
1619 |         [6, [7]],     // Locks, Locks Everywhere: P7
1620 |         [7, [8,9]],   // The Future, Ready Today: P8 + P9
1621 |       ]);
1622 |       let totalPads = 0;
1623 |       sections.forEach((sec, idx) => {
1624 |         let pad = sec.querySelector('.phase-pad');
1625 |         if (!pad) { pad = document.createElement('div'); pad.className = 'phase-pad'; sec.appendChild(pad); }
1626 |         let targetPx = 0;
1627 |         const phaseIds = mapping.get(idx);
1628 |         if (phaseIds){
1629 |           const ids = Array.isArray(phaseIds) ? phaseIds : [phaseIds];
1630 |           for (const id of ids) {
1631 |             const p = PHASES.find(pp => pp.id === id);
1632 |             if (p) targetPx += Math.max(0, Math.floor((p.end - p.start) * baseBudget));
1633 |           }
1634 |         }
1635 |         const needed = Math.max(0, targetPx);
1636 |         pad.style.height = needed + 'px';
1637 |         totalPads += needed;
1638 |       });
1639 |       // Offset pads by shrinking the spacer so total scroll stays aligned with the animation’s timeline
1640 |       if (spacer) {
1641 |         const minTail = 600; // keep extra tail so last sticky stays pinned through P9
1642 |         const newHeight = Math.max(minTail, baseBudget - totalPads + minTail);
1643 |         spacer.style.height = newHeight + 'px';
1644 |       }

### 1. Purpose and Functionality

The code `} }` represents the **closing braces** that terminate the JSON object structure in the English localization file. This is the final syntax that properly closes the entire JSON document, ensuring the file is valid JSON that can be parsed by JavaScript applications.

### 2. Key Components and Their Interactions

**JSON Structure Hierarchy:**
- **Root Object** (opened on line 1 with `{`): Contains all translation keys
- **Nested Objects**: Multiple child objects like `"nav"`, `"header"`, `"overlays"`, `"twinScience"`, etc.
- **Final Nested Object**: The `"comments"` object (lines 292-307) containing comment-related translations
- **Closing Sequence**: 
  - First `}` (line 307): Closes the `"comments"` object
  - Second `}` (line 308): Closes the root JSON object

**Interaction with Application:**
- This file is consumed by internationalization (i18n) systems
- The React application uses this JSON to display localized text
- The `RubiksIframe` component injects these translations into the iframe for the 3D animation
- The structure supports nested key access like `i18nResources.en.overlays["intro-1"].h1`

### 3. Important Patterns or Techniques Used

**JSON Object Literal Pattern:**
```json
{
  "key": "value",
  "nestedObject": {
    "subKey": "subValue"
  }
}
```

**Localization Key Organization:**
- **Flat Keys**: Simple translations like `"home": "Home"`
- **Nested Objects**: Complex structures like `"overlays"` containing multiple text blocks for the Rubik's cube animation
- **Template Variables**: Support for interpolation like `"backTo": "Back to {{topic}}"`

**Internationalization Architecture:**
- **Language-Specific Files**: Separate `en.json` and `ar.json` files
- **Key-Based Access**: Consistent keys across languages for reliable switching
- **Contextual Grouping**: Related translations grouped under logical sections (`nav`, `header`, `overlays`, etc.)

**Validation Requirements:**
- **Proper JSON Syntax**: Must be valid JSON to prevent parsing errors
- **UTF-8 Encoding**: Supports international characters (Arabic text in `ar.json`)
- **No Trailing Commas**: Strict JSON rules prevent syntax errors

This termination syntax is critical for the application's i18n system to function properly, as malformed JSON would cause the entire localization system to fail, resulting in missing text or application errors.</result>

  1 | import React, { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, forwardRef, useImperativeHandle } from 'react';
  2 | import { useTranslation } from 'react-i18next';
  3 | import enTranslations from '../locales/en.json';
  4 | import arTranslations from '../locales/ar.json';
  5 | 
  6 | interface RubiksIframeProps {
  7 |   height?: string;
  8 |   progress?: number | null; // 0..1 to externally drive the animation; null to let iframe use its own scroll
  9 |   onReady?: () => void;
 10 |   onProgress?: (value: number) => void;
 11 |   onPhaseChange?: (id: number, label: string) => void;
 12 | }
 13 | 
 14 | const RubiksIframe = forwardRef<HTMLIFrameElement, RubiksIframeProps>(
 15 |   ({ height = '100vh', progress = null, onReady, onProgress, onPhaseChange }, ref) => {
 16 |     const iframeRef = useRef<HTMLIFrameElement | null>(null);
 17 |     const resourcesInjectedRef = useRef(false);
 18 |     const initialLanguageRef = useRef<string | null>(null);
 19 |     useImperativeHandle(ref, () => iframeRef.current as HTMLIFrameElement, []);
 20 |     const { i18n } = useTranslation();
 21 | 
 22 |   const targetOrigin = useMemo(() => '*', []);
 23 | 
 24 |   // Inject i18n resources into iframe when it loads
 25 |   useEffect(() => {
 26 |     const iframe = iframeRef.current;
 27 |     if (!iframe) return;
 28 | 
 29 |     const handleLoad = () => {
 30 |       const win = iframe.contentWindow;
 31 |       if (!win) return;
 32 | 
 33 |       console.log('[RubiksIframe] Iframe loaded, injecting i18n resources');
 34 |       // Inject i18n resources
 35 |       (win as any).i18nResources = {
 36 |         en: enTranslations,
 37 |         ar: arTranslations
 38 |       };
 39 |       resourcesInjectedRef.current = true;
 40 |       initialLanguageRef.current = i18n.language;
 41 |       console.log('[RubiksIframe] i18n resources injected. Triggering initial render with language:', i18n.language);
 42 | 
 43 |       // Trigger initial render with current language
 44 |       win.postMessage({ type: 'RENDER_OVERLAYS', lang: i18n.language }, targetOrigin);
 45 |     };
 46 | 
 47 |     iframe.addEventListener('load', handleLoad);
 48 |     return () => {
 49 |       iframe.removeEventListener('load', handleLoad);
 50 |       resourcesInjectedRef.current = false;
 51 |       initialLanguageRef.current = null;
 52 |     };
 53 |   }, [targetOrigin, i18n.language]);
 54 | 
 55 |   // Listen to messages from the iframe
 56 |   useEffect(() => {
 57 |     function handleMessage(e: MessageEvent) {
 58 |       const data = e && (e.data as any);
 59 |       if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;
 60 |       if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_READY') {
 61 |         console.log('[RubiksIframe] Received RUBIKS_READY from iframe');
 62 |         onReady && onReady();
 63 |       } else if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_PROGRESS') {
 64 |         const v = Number(data.value);
 65 |         if (!Number.isNaN(v)) onProgress && onProgress(v);
 66 |       } else if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_PHASE') {
 67 |         const id = Number(data.id);
 68 |         const label = String(data.label ?? '');
 69 |         if (!Number.isNaN(id)) onPhaseChange && onPhaseChange(id, label);
 70 |       }
 71 |     }
 72 |     window.addEventListener('message', handleMessage);
 73 |     return () => window.removeEventListener('message', handleMessage);
 74 |   }, [onReady, onProgress, onPhaseChange]);
 75 | 
 76 |   // Send language change to iframe when language changes (but not on initial render)
 77 |   useEffect(() => {
 78 |     // Skip if this is the initial language or resources not injected yet
 79 |     if (!resourcesInjectedRef.current || initialLanguageRef.current === i18n.language) {
 80 |       return;
 81 |     }
 82 | 
 83 |     const win = iframeRef.current?.contentWindow;
 84 |     if (!win) return;
 85 |     
 86 |     console.log('[RubiksIframe] Language changed from', initialLanguageRef.current, 'to', i18n.language);
 87 |     initialLanguageRef.current = i18n.language;
 88 |     win.postMessage({ type: 'RENDER_OVERLAYS', lang: i18n.language }, targetOrigin);
 89 |   }, [i18n.language, targetOrigin]);
 90 | 
 91 |   // Push progress to the iframe when provided
 92 |   useEffect(() => {
 93 |     const win = iframeRef.current?.contentWindow;
 94 |     if (!win) return;
 95 |     if (progress === null || typeof progress === 'undefined') {
 96 |       win.postMessage({ type: 'RUBIKS_CLEAR_EXTERNAL' }, targetOrigin);
 97 |     } else {
 98 |       const v = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, Number(progress)));
 99 |       if (!Number.isNaN(v)) {
100 |         win.postMessage({ type: 'RUBIKS_SET_PROGRESS', value: v }, targetOrigin);
101 |       }
102 |     }
103 |   }, [progress, targetOrigin]);
104 | 
105 |     return (
106 |       <div style={{ position: 'relative', width: '100%', height }}>
107 |         <iframe
108 |           ref={iframeRef}
109 |           src="/rubiks-cdn.html"
110 |           title="Rubiks Animation"
111 |           style={{ position: 'absolute', inset: 0, width: '100%', height: '100%', border: 'none' }}
112 |           allow="autoplay; fullscreen; xr-spatial-tracking; clipboard-write"
113 |           sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-pointer-lock allow-top-navigation"
114 |         />
115 |       </div>
116 |     );
117 |   }
118 | );
119 | 
120 | export default RubiksIframe;
</content>

 376 |         <h1>Transforming Strategy Execution</h1>
 377 |         <h2>COMPLEXITY AS AN ASSET</h2>
 378 |         <p>Most transformations fail because complexity overwhelms. We turned that complexity into an advantage—redefining planning, risks, and dashboards inside one integrated model.</p>

 380 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 381 |         <h1>Imagine a Parallel Universe</h1>
 382 |         <h2>WHERE TRANSFORMATIONS<br>
 383 | FLOW</h2>
 384 |         <p>Let us show you a week in that universe — A Week in the Life of a Transformation Team &lt;video link&gt;. Farfetched? It’s here. We built the MVP: a Net.js web app with a Supabase database and a Gemini Assistant, built on a five-year scenario dataset inspired by real transformation events.</p>
 385 |       </div></section>
 386 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 387 |         <h1>So How Did We Do It?</h1>
 388 |         <h2>THE RIGHT QUESTIONS FIRST</h2>
 389 |         <p>Before answers, you need the right questions. This journey begins by uncovering the questions that matter most—the ones that unlock how complexity really works.</p>
 390 |       </div></section>
 391 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 392 |         <h1>The Anatomy of an Organization</h1>
 393 |         <h2>WHAT MAKES AN ORGANIZATION?</h2>
 394 |         <p>Many things, like a living system of systems—Strategy, Policies, Processes, Digital  shaped by external forces such as markets and global events. Real transformation means understanding how these components interact, not treating them in isolation.</p>
 395 |       </div></section>
 396 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 397 |         <h1>The Hidden Relations</h1>
 398 |         <h2>HOW DEEP DOES IT GO?</h2>
 399 |         <p>Each component has its own inputs, outputs, and hidden ties to others. When those ties are mapped, patterns emerge—a structure that shows why small changes ripple across the whole system.</p>

 428 |   <script type="module">
 429 |     /**
 430 |      * RUBIKS CUBE ANIMATION SYSTEM
 431 |      *
 432 |      * This script implements a complex 3D Rubik's cube animation with 9 distinct phases:
 433 |      * Phase 1: Idle/Gentle Float - Large cube with gentle rotation and hover
 434 |      * Phase 2: First Dismantle - Large pieces explode into cloud formation
 435 |      * Phase 3: Settle with Perspective - Pieces hover with random rotations
 436 |      * Phase 4: Rubik Transform - Large pieces shrink, mini-cubes (729 total) grow from within
 437 |      * Phase 5: Expand to 43.3% - Mini-cubes expand outward in cloud formation
 438 |      * Phase 6: Popcorn Recolor - Mini-cubes recolor from cyan to purple one-by-one
 439 |      * Phase 7: Dance - Mini-cubes swirl and orbit in complex patterns
 440 |      * Phase 8: Morph to Sculpture - Transform into final spherical sculpture
 441 |      * Phase 9: Final Formation - Interactive phase with mouse controls
 442 |      *
 443 |      * KEY COMPONENTS:
 444 |      * - 27 Large cubes (3x3x3) with metallic patterns and randomized face arrangements
 445 |      * - 729 Mini-cubes (27x27x27) with solid blue colors that recolor to purple
 446 |      * - Procedural texture generation for realistic sticker patterns
 447 |      * - Physically-based lighting and post-processing effects
 448 |      * - Scroll-driven animation with external control support
 449 |      * - Interactive mouse controls in phases 1 and 9
 450 |      */
 451 | 
 452 |     import * as THREE from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js';
 453 |    // import { OrbitControls } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js';
 454 |     import { EffectComposer } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js';
 455 |     import { RenderPass } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/RenderPass.js';
 456 |     import { UnrealBloomPass } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js';
 457 |     import { RoomEnvironment } from 'https://unpkg.com/three@0.180.0/examples/jsm/environments/RoomEnvironment.js';
 458 | 
 459 |     // Background video speed control
 460 |     const bgVideo = document.querySelector('.bg-video');
 461 |     const VIDEO_PLAYBACK_RATE = 0.4;
 462 |     function applyVideoSpeed() { 
 463 |       try { if (bgVideo) bgVideo.playbackRate = VIDEO_PLAYBACK_RATE; } catch(_){}
 464 |     }
 465 |     if (bgVideo) { bgVideo.addEventListener('loadeddata', applyVideoSpeed); bgVideo.addEventListener('play', applyVideoSpeed); }
 466 |     applyVideoSpeed();

 472 |       if (navPath && window.top) {

 477 |     function initializeNavigation() {

 481 |       });

 485 | 
 486 |     // ===== UTILITY FUNCTIONS =====
 487 |     /**
 488 |      * Mathematical utility functions for animation calculations
 489 |      */
 490 | 
 491 |     /**
 492 |      * Clamps a value between min and max bounds
 493 |      * @param {number} x - Value to clamp
 494 |      * @param {number} a - Minimum bound
 495 |      * @param {number} b - Maximum bound
 496 |      * @returns {number} Clamped value
 497 |      */
 498 |     const clamp = (x, a, b) => Math.max(a, Math.min(b, x));
 499 | 
 500 |     /**
 501 |      * Linear interpolation between two values
 502 |      * @param {number} a - Start value
 503 |      * @param {number} b - End value
 504 |      * @param {number} t - Interpolation factor (0-1)
 505 |      * @returns {number} Interpolated value
 506 |      */
 507 |     const lerp = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;
 508 | 
 509 |     /**
 510 |      * Inverse linear interpolation - finds t value for a point between a and b
 511 |      * @param {number} a - Start value
 512 |      * @param {number} b - End value
 513 |      * @param {number} v - Value to find t for
 514 |      * @returns {number} Interpolation factor (0-1)
 515 |      */
 516 |     const invLerp = (a, b, v) => clamp((v - a) / (b - a), 0, 1);
 517 | 
 518 |     /**
 519 |      * Smooth easing function for natural animation curves
 520 |      * Uses cubic easing for smooth acceleration/deceleration
 521 |      * @param {number} t - Input value (0-1)
 522 |      * @returns {number} Eased value (0-1)
 523 |      */
 524 |     const easeInOut = (t) => t < 0.5 ? 4*t*t*t : 1 - Math.pow(-2*t + 2, 3)/2;
 525 | 
 526 |     // ===== EXTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM =====
 527 |     /**
 528 |      * External progress control allows parent components to drive animation
 529 |      * Used by RubiksIframe component for programmatic control
 530 |      */
 531 | 
 532 |     /**
 533 |      * External progress override - when set, replaces scroll-based progress
 534 |      * @type {number|null} Value between 0-1, or null to use scroll
 535 |      */
 536 |     let externalProgress = null;
 537 | 
 538 |     /**
 539 |      * Message handler for external control from parent iframe
 540 |      * Supports two message types:
 541 |      * - RUBIKS_SET_PROGRESS: Set animation progress (0-1)
 542 |      * - RUBIKS_CLEAR_EXTERNAL: Return to scroll-based control
 543 |      */
 544 |     window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
 545 |       const data = e && e.data;
 546 |       if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;
 547 |       if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_SET_PROGRESS') {
 548 |         const v = Number(data.value);
 549 |         if (!Number.isNaN(v)) externalProgress = clamp(v, 0, 1);
 550 |       } else if (data.type === 'RUBIKS_CLEAR_EXTERNAL') {
 551 |         externalProgress = null;
 552 |       }
 553 |     });
 554 | 
 555 |     /**
 556 |      * Calculate progress within a specific phase range
 557 |      * @param {number} global - Global progress (0-1)
 558 |      * @param {number} a - Phase start point
 559 |      * @param {number} b - Phase end point
 560 |      * @returns {number} Local phase progress (0-1)
 561 |      */
 562 |     function phaseProgress(global, a, b) { return invLerp(a, b, global); }
 563 | 
 564 |     // ===== VIEWPORT AND CAMERA UTILITIES =====
 565 |     /**
 566 |      * Functions for calculating camera frustum and ensuring objects fit in view
 567 |      */
 568 | 
 569 |     /**
 570 |      * Calculate world-space half-extents of camera viewport at distance
 571 |      * @param {THREE.Camera} cam - Camera to calculate for
 572 |      * @returns {Object} Object with halfW and halfH properties
 573 |      */
 574 |     function viewportWorldHalfExtents(cam) {
 575 |       const d = cam.position.distanceTo(new THREE.Vector3());
 576 |       const halfH = Math.tan(THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(cam.fov * 0.5)) * d;
 577 |       const halfW = halfH * cam.aspect;
 578 |       return { halfW, halfH };
 579 |     }
 580 | 
 581 |     /**
 582 |      * Normalized device coordinate padding - allows full viewport usage
 583 |      * Value of 1.0 means no safety margin, objects can touch viewport edges
 584 |      */
 585 |     const PAD_NDC = 1.0; // allow full viewport usage (no extra safety margin)
 586 | 
 587 |     /**
 588 |      * Generate all 8 corners of a cube
 589 |      * @param {THREE.Vector3} center - Cube center position
 590 |      * @param {number} half - Half-size of cube
 591 |      * @returns {THREE.Vector3[]} Array of 8 corner positions
 592 |      */
 593 |     function cubeCorners(center, half) {
 594 |       const offs = [-1, 1];
 595 |       const res = [];
 596 |       for (const dx of offs) for (const dy of offs) for (const dz of offs) {
 597 |         res.push(new THREE.Vector3(center.x + dx*half, center.y + dy*half, center.z + dz*half));
 598 |       }
 599 |       return res;
 600 |     }
 601 | 
 602 |     /**
 603 |      * Check if a cube fits entirely within the camera viewport
 604 |      * @param {THREE.Vector3} center - Cube center position
 605 |      * @param {number} half - Half-size of cube
 606 |      * @returns {boolean} True if cube fits in view
 607 |      */
 608 |     function cornersFitInView(center, half) {
 609 |       const corners = cubeCorners(center, half);
 610 |       for (const c of corners) {
 611 |         const p = c.clone().project(camera);
 612 |         if (Math.abs(p.x) > PAD_NDC || Math.abs(p.y) > PAD_NDC || p.z < -1 || p.z > 1) return false;
 613 |       }
 614 |       return true;
 615 |     }
 616 | 
 617 |     /**
 618 |      * Find maximum scale along a direction that keeps cube in viewport
 619 |      * Uses binary search to find optimal position
 620 |      * @param {THREE.Vector3} dir - Direction vector
 621 |      * @param {number} R - Maximum radius to search
 622 |      * @param {number} half - Half-size of cube
 623 |      * @returns {number} Maximum scale factor that keeps cube in view
 624 |      */
 625 |     function clampAlongDirToFit(dir, R, half) {
 626 |       // binary search max s in [0, R] such that corners fit
 627 |       let lo = 0, hi = R;
 628 |       for (let it = 0; it < 20; it++) {
 629 |         const mid = (lo + hi) * 0.5;
 630 |         const pos = dir.clone().multiplyScalar(mid);
 631 |         if (cornersFitInView(pos, half)) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
 632 |       }
 633 |       return lo;
 634 |     }
 635 | 
 636 |     // ===== PROCEDURAL TEXTURE GENERATION SYSTEM =====
 637 |     /**
 638 |      * Dynamic texture creation for cube faces with various patterns and colors
 639 |      *
 640 |      * PATTERN SYSTEM:
 641 |      * - 6 distinct pattern types: grid, stripes, ring, chevron, hex, wave
 642 |      * - Each pattern is procedurally generated on 512x512 canvas
 643 |      * - Navy blue color palette with gradient backgrounds
 644 |      * - Optional gloss effects for metallic appearance
 645 |      *
 646 |      * RANDOMIZATION:
 647 |      * - Large cubes: Each gets 6 shuffled patterns, one per face
 648 |      * - Mini cubes: Each gets 6 shuffled patterns, one per face
 649 |      * - Colors: 6 different blue shades for visual variety
 650 |      *
 651 |      * CACHING:
 652 |      * - Textures are cached to avoid recreation on each frame
 653 |      * - Large and mini textures cached separately
 654 |      * - Canvas-based generation for crisp, scalable results
 655 |      */
 656 |     const STICKER_CACHE = { largeTexs: null, miniTexs: null };
 657 |     const FACE_PATTERNS = ['grid','stripes','ring','chevron','hex','wave'];
 658 |     const BLUES = ['#000033','#000066','#000099','#0000CC','#000033','#000066'];
 659 | 
 660 |     let fixedFaceAssignments = [];
 661 | 
 662 |     fetch('/faces.json')
 663 |       .then(response => response.json())
 664 |       .then(data => {
 665 |         fixedFaceAssignments = data.faces.map(face => face.pattern);
 666 |       })
 667 |       .catch(error => console.error('Error loading face patterns:', error));
 668 | 
 669 |     /**
 670 |      * Create a procedural sticker texture with pattern and optional gloss
 671 |      * @param {string} pattern - Pattern type: 'grid', 'stripes', 'ring', 'chevron', 'hex', 'wave'
 672 |      * @param {string} baseHex - Base color in hex format (e.g., '#000066')
 673 |      * @param {boolean} drawPatterns - Whether to draw the pattern overlay
 674 |      * @param {boolean} drawGloss - Whether to add gloss/highlight effect
 675 |      * @returns {THREE.CanvasTexture} Generated texture for Three.js
 676 |      */
 677 |     function createStickerTexture(pattern, baseHex, drawPatterns = true, drawGloss = true){
 678 |       const size = 512; // High resolution for crisp textures
 679 |       const c = document.createElement('canvas');
 680 |       c.width = c.height = size;
 681 |       const ctx = c.getContext('2d');
 682 | 
 683 |       // Create gradient background for depth
 684 |       const grad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,size,size);
 685 |       grad.addColorStop(0, baseHex); // Primary color
 686 |       grad.addColorStop(1, shadeHex(baseHex, -20)); // Darker shade for depth
 687 |       ctx.fillStyle = grad;
 688 |       ctx.fillRect(0,0,size,size);
 689 | 
 690 |       // Inner rounded rectangle for sticker inset effect
 691 |       const inset = Math.floor(size * 0.08); // 8% inset from edges
 692 |       roundedRect(ctx, inset, inset, size-2*inset, size-2*inset, Math.floor(size*0.06));
 693 |       ctx.fillStyle = shadeHex(baseHex, -35); // Even darker for inset shadow
 694 |       ctx.globalAlpha = 0.22; // Semi-transparent inset
 695 |       ctx.fill();
 696 |       ctx.globalAlpha = 1; // Reset alpha
 697 |       // ===== PATTERN DRAWING SYSTEM =====
 698 |       /**
 699 |        * Draw specific pattern on the texture
 700 |        * Each pattern is centered and uses white strokes with drop shadows
 701 |        * for raised 3D appearance
 702 |        */
 703 |       const drawPattern = (name) => {
 704 |         ctx.save();
 705 |         ctx.translate(size/2, size/2); // Center coordinate system
 706 |         ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,1.0)'; // Pure white for maximum contrast
 707 |         ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.3)'; // Semi-transparent white for fills
 708 |         ctx.lineWidth = Math.max(8, size*0.015); // Responsive line width
 709 | 
 710 |         // Drop shadow for raised 3D effect
 711 |         ctx.shadowColor = 'rgba(0,0,0,1.0)';
 712 |         ctx.shadowBlur = Math.max(12, size*0.03);
 713 |         ctx.shadowOffsetX = Math.max(5, size*0.01);
 714 |         ctx.shadowOffsetY = Math.max(5, size*0.01);
 715 |         // ===== INDIVIDUAL PATTERN IMPLEMENTATIONS =====
 716 | 
 717 |         if (name === 'grid') {
 718 |           // Grid pattern: Regular intersecting lines
 719 |           ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,0.8)';
 720 |           const step = Math.floor(size/10); // 10 divisions
 721 |           // Vertical lines
 722 |           for(let x=inset; x<=size-inset; x+=step){
 723 |             ctx.beginPath();
 724 |             ctx.moveTo(x,inset);
 725 |             ctx.lineTo(x,size-inset);
 726 |             ctx.stroke();
 727 |           }
 728 |           // Horizontal lines
 729 |           for(let y=inset; y<=size-inset; y+=step){
 730 |             ctx.beginPath();
 731 |             ctx.moveTo(inset,y);
 732 |             ctx.lineTo(size-inset,y);
 733 |             ctx.stroke();
 734 |           }
 735 |         } else if (name === 'stripes') {
 736 |           // Diagonal stripe pattern
 737 |           ctx.rotate(-Math.PI/6); // 30-degree angle
 738 |           for(let i=-6;i<=6;i++){
 739 |             ctx.beginPath();
 740 |             ctx.moveTo(-size, i*32);
 741 |             ctx.lineTo(size, i*32);
 742 |             ctx.stroke();
 743 |           }
 744 |         } else if (name === 'ring') {
 745 |           // Concentric ring pattern
 746 |           ctx.beginPath();
 747 |           ctx.arc(0,0,size*0.28,0,Math.PI*2); // Outer ring
 748 |           ctx.stroke();
 749 |           ctx.beginPath();
 750 |           ctx.arc(0,0,size*0.14,0,Math.PI*2); // Inner ring
 751 |           ctx.stroke();
 752 |         } else if (name === 'chevron') {
 753 |           // Chevron/V pattern
 754 |           for(let i=0;i<4;i++){
 755 |             const off = -size*0.15 + i*size*0.1;
 756 |             ctx.beginPath();
 757 |             ctx.moveTo(-size*0.25, off);
 758 |             ctx.lineTo(0, off+size*0.08);
 759 |             ctx.lineTo(size*0.25, off);
 760 |             ctx.stroke();
 761 |           }
 762 |         } else if (name === 'hex') {
 763 |           // Hexagon pattern
 764 |           const r = size*0.22;
 765 |           ctx.beginPath();
 766 |           for(let i=0;i<6;i++){
 767 |             const a = Math.PI/3*i; // 60-degree increments
 768 |             const x = r*Math.cos(a), y=r*Math.sin(a);
 769 |             if(i===0) ctx.moveTo(x,y); else ctx.lineTo(x,y);
 770 |           }
 771 |           ctx.closePath();
 772 |           ctx.stroke();
 773 |         } else if (name === 'wave') {
 774 |           // Sine wave pattern
 775 |           ctx.translate(-size*0.3, 0);
 776 |           for(let i=-3;i<=3;i++){
 777 |             ctx.beginPath();
 778 |             for(let x=-size*0.2; x<=size*0.2; x+=8){
 779 |               const y = Math.sin((x/50)+i)*size*0.04;
 780 |               if (x===-size*0.2) ctx.moveTo(x,y); else ctx.lineTo(x,y);
 781 |             }
 782 |             ctx.stroke();
 783 |           }
 784 |         }
 785 |         ctx.restore();
 786 |       };
 787 |       // Apply pattern and gloss effects
 788 |       if (drawPatterns) drawPattern(pattern);
 789 | 
 790 |       if (drawGloss) {
 791 |         // ===== GLOSS/HIGHLIGHT EFFECT =====
 792 |         // Creates metallic shine effect on upper portion of texture
 793 |         const gloss = ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,0,size);
 794 |         gloss.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.22)'); // Bright highlight at top
 795 |         gloss.addColorStop(0.5, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.08)'); // Fade to middle
 796 |         gloss.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.0)'); // Transparent at bottom
 797 |         ctx.fillStyle = gloss;
 798 |         roundedRect(ctx, inset, inset, size-2*inset, Math.floor((size-2*inset)*0.55), Math.floor(size*0.06));
 799 |         ctx.fill();
 800 |       }
 801 | 
 802 |       // ===== TEXTURE CREATION AND OPTIMIZATION =====
 803 |       const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
 804 |       tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace; // Standard RGB color space
 805 |       tex.anisotropy = 8; // Anisotropic filtering for better quality at angles
 806 |       tex.needsUpdate = true; // Mark for GPU upload
 807 |       return tex;
 808 |     }
 809 |     // ===== UTILITY FUNCTIONS =====
 810 | 
 811 |     /**
 812 |      * Shuffle array in-place using Fisher-Yates algorithm
 813 |      * Used to randomize pattern order for visual variety
 814 |      * @param {Array} array - Array to shuffle
 815 |      * @returns {Array} Same array, shuffled in place
 816 |      */
 817 |     function shuffle(array) {
 818 |       for (let i = array.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
 819 |         const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
 820 |         [array[i], array[j]] = [array[j], array[i]];
 821 |       }
 822 |       return array;
 823 |     }
 824 | 
 825 |     /**
 826 |      * Draw rounded rectangle path on canvas
 827 |      * @param {CanvasRenderingContext2D} ctx - Canvas context
 828 |      * @param {number} x - X position
 829 |      * @param {number} y - Y position
 830 |      * @param {number} w - Width
 831 |      * @param {number} h - Height
 832 |      * @param {number} r - Corner radius
 833 |      */
 834 |     function roundedRect(ctx,x,y,w,h,r){
 835 |       ctx.beginPath();
 836 |       ctx.moveTo(x+r,y);
 837 |       ctx.arcTo(x+w,y,x+w,y+h,r);
 838 |       ctx.arcTo(x+w,y+h,x,y+h,r);
 839 |       ctx.arcTo(x,y+h,x,y,r);
 840 |       ctx.arcTo(x,y,x+w,y,r);
 841 |       ctx.closePath();
 842 |     }
 843 | 
 844 |     /**
 845 |      * Shade hex color by adding/subtracting brightness
 846 |      * @param {string} hex - Hex color string (with or without #)
 847 |      * @param {number} amt - Amount to add/subtract (-255 to 255)
 848 |      * @returns {string} New hex color string
 849 |      */
 850 |     function shadeHex(hex, amt){
 851 |       const c = hex.startsWith('#') ? hex.substring(1) : hex;
 852 |       const num = parseInt(c,16);
 853 |       const r = Math.min(255, Math.max(0, ((num>>16)&0xff) + amt));
 854 |       const g = Math.min(255, Math.max(0, ((num>>8)&0xff) + amt));
 855 |       const b = Math.min(255, Math.max(0, (num&0xff) + amt));
 856 |       return `#${(r<<16|g<<8|b).toString(16).padStart(6,'0')}`;
 857 |     }
 858 |     /**
 859 |      * Get cached textures for large cubes with full patterns and gloss
 860 |      * @returns {THREE.CanvasTexture[]} Array of 6 textures, one per pattern
 861 |      */
 862 |     function getLargeStickerTextures(){
 863 |       if (STICKER_CACHE.largeTexs) return STICKER_CACHE.largeTexs;
 864 |       const texs = FACE_PATTERNS.map((pat, i) => createStickerTexture(pat, BLUES[i%BLUES.length], true, true));
 865 |       STICKER_CACHE.largeTexs = texs;
 866 |       return texs;
 867 |     }
 868 | 
 869 |     /**
 870 |      * Get cached textures for mini cubes with solid colors (no patterns, no gloss)
 871 |      * @returns {THREE.CanvasTexture[]} Array of 6 solid color textures
 872 |      */
 873 |     function getMiniStickerTextures(){
 874 |       if (STICKER_CACHE.miniTexs) return STICKER_CACHE.miniTexs;
 875 |       const texs = FACE_PATTERNS.map((pat, i) => createStickerTexture(pat, BLUES[i%BLUES.length], false, false));
 876 |       STICKER_CACHE.miniTexs = texs;
 877 |       return texs;
 878 |     }
 879 |     function addStickers(mesh, size){
 880 |       const s = size * 0.94; // slight inset
 881 |       const offset = size/2 + 0.02;
 882 |       const mats = getLargeStickerMaterials();
 883 |       const planes = [];
 884 |       const geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(s, s);
 885 |       const dirs = [
 886 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 1, 0, 0), rot: [0, -Math.PI/2, 0] }, // +X
 887 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3(-1, 0, 0), rot: [0,  Math.PI/2, 0] }, // -X
 888 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0, 1, 0), rot: [ Math.PI/2, 0, 0] }, // +Y
 889 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0,-1, 0), rot: [-Math.PI/2, 0, 0] }, // -Y
 890 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0, 0, 1), rot: [0, 0, 0] },           // +Z
 891 |         { n: new THREE.Vector3( 0, 0,-1), rot: [0,  Math.PI, 0] },    // -Z
 892 |       ];
 893 |       dirs.forEach((d, i) => {
 894 |         const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mats[i]);
 895 |         m.position.copy(d.n.clone().multiplyScalar(offset));

 898 |         m.userData.sticker = true;

 900 |         mesh.add(m);
 901 |         planes.push(m);
 902 |       });
 903 |       return planes;

 906 |     // ===== CUBE CREATION SYSTEM =====
 907 |     /**
 908 |      * Create a cube with size-appropriate materials and geometry
 909 |      *
 910 |      * SIZE-BASED MATERIAL SYSTEM:
 911 |      * - Large cubes (>0.99): MeshStandardMaterial with metallic properties and shuffled patterns
 912 |      * - Mini cubes (0.1-0.99): MeshBasicMaterial with solid blue colors for recoloring
 913 |      * - Tiny cubes (<0.1): MeshPhysicalMaterial with metallic properties
 914 |      *
 915 |      * MATERIAL PROPERTIES:
 916 |      * - Large: metalness=0.2, roughness=0.6, polygon offset for depth sorting
 917 |      * - Mini: Basic material for efficient recoloring during Phase 6
 918 |      * - Tiny: High metalness/roughness for metallic appearance
 919 |      *
 920 |      * EDGE SYSTEM:
 921 |      * - All cubes get LineSegments edges with dark navy color (#000033)
 922 |      * - Edges render on top (renderOrder=10) for crisp outlines
 923 |      * - Edges are added as children of the mesh for proper transformation
 924 |      *
 925 |      * @param {number} size - Cube size (determines material type)
 926 |      * @param {number} fillColor - Fill color for tiny cubes
 927 |      * @param {number} edgeColor - Edge color (typically dark navy)
 928 |      * @returns {THREE.Mesh} Configured cube mesh with edges
 929 |      */
 930 |     function makeCube(size, fillColor, edgeColor, cubeIndex = 0) {
 931 |       const geom = new THREE.BoxGeometry(size, size, size);
 932 |       let mesh;
 933 | 
 934 |       if (size > 0.1) {
 935 |         if (size >= 0.99) {
 936 |           // ===== LARGE CUBE CREATION =====
 937 |           // 27 large cubes forming the initial Rubik's cube structure
 938 |           const pats = fixedFaceAssignments.length > 0 ? fixedFaceAssignments.slice() : shuffle(FACE_PATTERNS.slice()); // Randomize pattern order per cube
 939 |           // Load all 6 bump map textures
 940 |           const bumpTextures = [1,2,3,4,5,6].map(n => {
 941 |             const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load(`/assets/textures/cubeface${n}.png`);
 942 |             tex.wrapS = THREE.RepeatWrapping;
 943 |             tex.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping;
 944 |             tex.repeat.set(1, 1);
 945 |             return tex;
 946 |           });
 947 |           // Randomly assign bump map to each face
 948 |           const mats = pats.map((pat, i) => new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
 949 |             // map: createStickerTexture(pat, BLUES[i%BLUES.length], true, true), // Pattern overlay commented out
 950 |             color: new THREE.Color(fillColor), // Use the fillColor parameter instead of hardcoded value
 951 |             bumpMap: bumpTextures[Math.floor(Math.random()*6)],
 952 |             bumpScale: 1.0, // Maximum bump effect
 953 |             transparent: false, // Opaque for performance
 954 |             depthWrite: false, // Disable depth writing to prevent z-fighting
 955 |             depthTest: true, // Still test depth for proper ordering
 956 |             side: THREE.DoubleSide, // Render both sides (important for cube faces)
 957 |             metalness: 1.0, // Fully metallic
 958 |             roughness: 0.1, // Very shiny
 959 |             polygonOffset: true, // Offset depth to prevent z-fighting with edges
 960 |             polygonOffsetFactor: -4,
 961 |             polygonOffsetUnits: -4
 962 |           }));
 963 |           mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, mats); // Array of 6 materials, one per face
 964 |         } else {
 965 |           // ===== MINI CUBE CREATION =====
 966 |           // 729 mini cubes that emerge from within large cubes
 967 |          // const miniMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
 968 |           // --- ORIGINAL MINI CUBE MATERIAL CREATION (commented out) ---
 969 |           // const miniMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
 970 |           //   color: new THREE.Color(0x0066CC), // Blue color for mini-cubes
 971 |           //   transparent: false, // Opaque
 972 |           //   opacity: 1.0, // Fully opaque
 973 |           //   depthWrite: true, // Enable depth writing to prevent see-through
 974 |           //   depthTest: true, // Test depth
 975 |           //   side: THREE.DoubleSide, // Render both sides
 976 |           //   metalness: 0.25, // Balanced metallic feel
 977 |           //   roughness: 0.5 // Balanced surface roughness
 978 |           // });
 979 |           // mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, miniMaterial); // Single metallic material for all faces
 980 | 
 981 |           // --- MINI CUBE MATERIAL WITH NO GLOW/EMISSIVE ---
 982 |           const miniMaterial = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
 983 |             color: new THREE.Color(0x0066CC),
 984 |             transparent: false,
 985 |             opacity: 1.0,
 986 |             depthWrite: true,
 987 |             depthTest: true,
 988 |             side: THREE.DoubleSide,
 989 |             metalness: 0.25,
 990 |             roughness: 0.5,
 991 |             emissive: new THREE.Color(0x000000), // No glow
 992 |             emissiveIntensity: 0.0 // No glow
 993 |           });
 994 |           mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, miniMaterial); // Single metallic material for all faces
 995 |         }
 996 |       } else {
 997 |         // ===== TINY CUBE CREATION =====
 998 |         // Smallest cubes in final sculpture formation
 999 |         const mat = new THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial({
1000 |           color: fillColor,
1001 |           metalness: 1.0, // Highly metallic
1002 |           roughness: 0.25, // Smooth surface
1003 |           clearcoat: 1.0, // Clear coat layer for extra shine
1004 |           clearcoatRoughness: 0.15, // Smooth clear coat
1005 | //          envMapIntensity: 1.2 // Environment reflection intensity
1006 |         });
1007 |         mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, mat); // Single material for all faces
1008 |       }
1009 |       // ===== MESH CONFIGURATION =====
1010 |       mesh.castShadow = true; // Cast shadows for depth
1011 |       mesh.receiveShadow = true; // Receive shadows from other objects
1012 | 
1013 |       // ===== EDGE CREATION =====
1014 |       // Add edges for all cubes, but make mini-cube edges very thin
1015 |       const edges = new THREE.LineSegments(
1016 |         new THREE.EdgesGeometry(geom), // Extract edges from box geometry
1017 |         new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({
1018 |           color: edgeColor, // Use provided edge color
1019 |           linewidth: size >= 0.99 ? 1 : 0.5 // Thin lines for mini-cubes
1020 |         })
1021 |       );
1022 |       edges.renderOrder = 10; // Render edges on top of faces
1023 |       mesh.add(edges); // Add as child so edges follow mesh transformations
1024 | 
1025 |       return mesh;
1026 |     }

1028 |     /**
1029 |      * Set fill color for all meshes in a 3D object hierarchy
1030 |      * Used for global color changes during different animation phases
1031 |      * @param {THREE.Object3D} obj3D - Root object to traverse
1032 |      * @param {number} color - Color value (hex number)
1033 |      */
1034 |     function setCubeFillColor(obj3D, color) {
1035 |       obj3D.traverse(o => {
1036 |         if (o.isMesh && o.material) {
1037 |           if (Array.isArray(o.material)) {
1038 |             // Handle multi-material meshes (cubes with different face materials)
1039 |             o.material.forEach(m => { if (m && m.color) m.color.set(color); });
1040 |           } else {
1041 |             // Handle single-material meshes
1042 |             if (o.material.color) o.material.color.set(color);
1043 |           }
1044 |         }
1045 |       });
1046 |     }

1267 |             miniGroup.add(m);

 244 |             return window.parent.document.documentElement.lang;

 248 |         if (params.get('lang')) return params.get('lang');

 250 |       }
 251 | function renderOverlays(forceLang) {
 252 |   let lang = forceLang || getLang();
 253 |   lang = lang && lang.startsWith('ar') ? 'ar' : 'en';
 254 |   console.log('[renderOverlays] Step 1: Language =', lang);
 255 |   
 256 |   const overlays = getI18n(lang);

 297 |                   </div>

 299 |               </div>

 304 |                 <h1>${data.h1}</h1>
 305 |                 <h2>${data.h2}</h2>
 306 |                 <p>${data.p}</p>
 307 |               </div>
 308 |             `;
 309 |           }
 310 |         });  //this closes forEach

 312 |         overlayInner.innerHTML.length);
 313 | 
 314 |   console.log('[renderOverlays] Final HTML =', overlayInner.innerHTML.length, 'chars');
 315 |

 371 |     <div class="hero-row">
 372 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 373 |         <h1>Transforming Strategy Execution</h1>
 374 |         <h2>COMPLEXITY AS AN ASSET</h2>
 375 |         <p>Most transformations fail because complexity overwhelms. We turned that complexity into an advantage—redefining planning, risks, and dashboards inside one integrated model.</p>
 376 |       </div></section>
 377 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 378 |         <h1>Imagine a Parallel Universe</h1>
 379 |         <h2>WHERE TRANSFORMATIONS<br>
 380 | FLOW</h2>
 381 |         <p>Let us show you a week in that universe — A Week in the Life of a Transformation Team &lt;video link&gt;. Farfetched? It’s here. We built the MVP: a Net.js web app with a Supabase database and a Gemini Assistant, built on a five-year scenario dataset inspired by real transformation events.</p>
 382 |       </div></section>
 383 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 384 |         <h1>So How Did We Do It?</h1>
 385 |         <h2>THE RIGHT QUESTIONS FIRST</h2>
 386 |         <p>Before answers, you need the right questions. This journey begins by uncovering the questions that matter most—the ones that unlock how complexity really works.</p>
 387 |       </div></section>
 388 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 389 |         <h1>The Anatomy of an Organization</h1>
 390 |         <h2>WHAT MAKES AN ORGANIZATION?</h2>
 391 |         <p>Many things, like a living system of systems—Strategy, Policies, Processes, Digital  shaped by external forces such as markets and global events. Real transformation means understanding how these components interact, not treating them in isolation.</p>
 392 |       </div></section>
 393 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 394 |         <h1>The Hidden Relations</h1>
 395 |         <h2>HOW DEEP DOES IT GO?</h2>
 396 |         <p>Each component has its own inputs, outputs, and hidden ties to others. When those ties are mapped, patterns emerge—a structure that shows why small changes ripple across the whole system.</p>
 397 |       </div></section>
 398 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 399 |         <h1>The Moment of Truth</h1>
 400 |         <h2>SHOULD YOU WALK THIS JOURNEY?</h2>
 401 |         <p>We already did—and the answer is yes. But do it with eyes open. Complexity runs deeper than expected, and guidance is scarce. That’s why we built a model that captures the whole picture and makes the path navigable.</p>
 402 |       </div></section>
 403 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 404 |         <h1>Locks, Locks Everywhere</h1>
 405 |         <h2>WHAT DID 2 YEARS REVEAL?</h2>
 406 |         <p>Unlock after unlock, the journey was long and often tedious. Every piece had to be dissected, connected, and validated until a full digital twin of dependencies emerged. Just as we reached this milestone, AI leapt forward—suddenly powerful, affordable, and accessible—turning what seemed impossible into reality.</p>
 407 |       </div></section>
 408 |       <section class="text-section"><div class="text-col">
 409 |         <h1>The Future, Ready Today</h1>
 410 |         <h2>WHAT PATH WILL YOU CHOOSE?</h2>
 411 |         <p>With the AI core in place, the Digital Twin comes alive. We’ve hit a milestone, but the journey is still unfolding. Two paths now await: a Knowledge Path, where you contribute ideas and shape the future of transformations; and a Builder Path, where you begin your own strategy execution journey and put the twin to work.</p>
 412 |       </div></section>
